summary: No reachable path lets candidate code read, replace, predict or impersonate the sealed expected reports or the reward. Candidate code only runs in the verifier as uid 65534 under no_new_privs with a cleared environment. It uses a verifier-owned driver copy, neutral input paths and random working directories, and it cannot read the root-only /tests and /logs/verifier. The reward is written by root from pytest's exit code.
checks_performed: Compared the packet manifest's 41 listed files with the files read; all were read in full, with no truncation.
Traced agent-image contents: environment/Dockerfile:6 copies only app/, and environment/.dockerignore:11-12 excludes solution/ and tests/, so no goldens or reference reach the candidate container.

Traced verifier image setup: tests/Dockerfile:5-12 places tests at /tests (root, mode 700). It installs a root-owned driver copy at /opt/driver/tools (dir 755, file 644), whose src is a root-owned symlink to /app/src.

Traced test.sh ordering: test.sh:4-5 sets /logs/verifier to 700 and writes reward 0. test.sh:15 re-seals /tests and /logs/verifier before any candidate code runs. test.sh:18-26 runs pytest from a fresh mktemp dir and writes the reward as root from pytest rc only.

Traced candidate execution: test_outputs.py:61-82 runs setpriv with --reuid/--regid 65534, --clear-groups and --no-new-privs, plus env -i with a fixed PATH/HOME/LANG, in a new session, killing the group afterwards. test_outputs.py:85-99 runs python3 -I -S on the verifier-owned driver with a neutral path <mkdtemp>/batch.json in a random working directory.

Checked that the driver (tests/shipped/tools/metalquant_run.py:7-18) imports only the candidate package through /opt/driver/src and prints its JSON to stdout. Root pytest parses only that stdout (test_outputs.py:99) and compares it with sealed goldens (test_outputs.py:102-130).

Checked root reads of candidate-controlled paths: the only one is test_outputs.py:206, DELIVERED_DRIVER read_bytes. Following a symlink there can at best make the byte-equality pass, which leaving the file untouched also achieves. Grading uses the verifier's own driver copy, so this gives no credit without doing the task.
Checked chmod -R a+rX /app (test.sh:16): recursive GNU chmod does not follow symlinks met during traversal, so a symlink planted in /app cannot open up /tests or /logs.

Checked answer leakage through inputs: every batch payload in all 18 jsonl families holds only SOP section-1 fields. Run ids (W-31, MB-1, CCV-1, R282-0, ...) do not encode flags, pass verdicts or values. The file name, working directory, argv and environment are identical in form for every family.
Checked integrity of goldens: load() pins each file's SHA-256 and row count from ROSTER (test_outputs.py:38-58). ROSTER and the goldens are both under root-only /tests.

Checked malformed-output edge cases in the trusted comparator: NaN/Infinity fail the tolerance check (test_outputs.py:104-105), bools are excluded (test_outputs.py:103), and null is accepted only where expected (test_outputs.py:122-125). None of these can turn a wrong answer into a pass.
Checked the verifier's own access probes: test_outputs.py:209-220 confirms from the candidate uid that /tests/expected/ROSTER and /logs/verifier are unreadable.

coverage_sweep.category: Expected answers and live reference implementations inaccessible to candidate code, including code the verifier executes
coverage_sweep.reason: Goldens live only in the verifier image under /tests, mode 700 root. Candidate code runs as uid 65534 with no_new_privs. No solution files are in either image (.dockerignore, tests/Dockerfile COPY of the tests context only). The agent image contains only app/.

coverage_sweep.category: Privileged reads of candidate-influenced paths (symlink / path traversal)
coverage_sweep.reason: Root reads of candidate-controlled paths are limited to the delivered-driver byte comparison and chmod -R over /app. The symlink-follow in the comparison gives no credit beyond leaving the file unchanged. chmod -R does not follow symlinks during traversal. The batch input is written by root into a root-owned 755 stage dir, which the candidate cannot replace.

coverage_sweep.category: Expected values computed independently of the submitted artifact
coverage_sweep.reason: Expected reports are precomputed, sealed jsonl files with digests pinned in ROSTER. Nothing derives the expectation from candidate output or a candidate-supplied checksum.

coverage_sweep.category: Hidden outcomes exposed through filenames, arguments, working directories or environment variables
coverage_sweep.reason: Every batch is passed as <random mkdtemp>/batch.json and run from another random mkdtemp. The environment is cleared to fixed values and argv is fixed. Batch contents carry only SOP fields and outcome-neutral run ids.

coverage_sweep.category: Grading results kept in a trusted channel (candidate stdout / early exit cannot impersonate verification)
coverage_sweep.reason: Candidate stdout is only data, parsed as JSON and compared field by field with sealed goldens. The reward is written by root from pytest's exit code into /logs/verifier, which is 700 and not writable by uid 65534. Candidate exit code 0 alone gives no credit.

coverage_sweep.category: Access boundary tested from the candidate's execution context; suspected shortcuts confirmed defeated
coverage_sweep.reason: The verifier probes readability of ROSTER and /logs/verifier through the same run_unprivileged wrapper used for candidate code. A lingering double-forked uid-65534 process could escape killpg, but it cannot write /tests, /logs/verifier or the root-owned stage files, and cannot signal root pytest. It has no answer-bearing state to use.

coverage_sweep.category: Persisted / cached state and colocated oracle binaries (cache_carryover, colocation_walk)
coverage_sweep.reason: No reference implementation is in the verifier image. The only verifier-owned executable reachable by the candidate is the unchanged shipped driver. No validated result is stored back in candidate-writable state and reused as an expectation.

coverage_sweep.category: Privilege-drop bypass via setuid (chmod_follow C-3 pattern)
coverage_sweep.reason: setpriv is invoked with --no-new-privs, and the verifier never installs candidate files as setuid.

rules: instruction: batches are reduced by our own copy of the driver against your /app/src
verifier: driver src symlink resolves into candidate-controlled /app/src
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: The candidate makes /app/src a symlink or plants code in it. The code is imported only by the unprivileged driver process (python3 -I -S). Even a symlink to /tests gains nothing because uid 65534 cannot traverse /tests (700 root).

rules: verifier: root reads the delivered driver path
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: The candidate replaces /app/tools/metalquant_run.py with a symlink to the shipped copy. The root read follows it and the equality passes. This is the same outcome as leaving the file unchanged, and grading never runs the delivered driver.

rules: test.sh makes /app world-readable before candidate runs
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Order check: the chmod 700 of /tests and /logs/verifier (line 15) comes before chmod -R a+rX /app (line 16). Symlinks inside /app are not followed by recursive chmod, so the widening cannot reach the sealed directories.

rules: multiple families run sequentially in one verifier session
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A lingering candidate process that counts invocations or reads earlier stage dirs (0755, batch inputs only) learns only inputs, never expected reports. It therefore cannot swap in precomputed answers.
